items.value: When writing execution plans, be detailed and provide context plus firm implementation direction. Plans should be consumable by another model starting from zero context and executable correctly.
Prefer concise explanations that avoid reading fatigue. Do not include every detail for its own sake; use compact structure and visual aids like tables/graphs/illustrations when helpful.

NEVER write, create, edit, comment, close, publish, upload, or otherwise mutate anything on an external service without explicit permission for that exact external action. Always assume artifacts should remain local. Ask permission immediately before any external write, even if the user approved the content, said proceed, invoked a workflow, or external tooling/configuration is available.

All Pi skills should live in ~/.agents/skills. ~/.pi/agent/skills should not store separate skill copies; avoid per-skill symlinks there because Pi scans both global roots and creates name-collision warnings. Pi config sync should sync only user-authored skills from ~/.agents/skills, excluding .skill-lock package-managed skills.

When using pi, the user prefers a step-by-step workflow by default: diagnose/explain first, ask before making fixes or taking action, especially when the request is framed as a question or investigation.

In ~/pi-config-sync, only user-authored skills should be synced. Current allowlist is MANAGED_SKILL_DIRS = ["triage-review-comment", "dissect-plan"] in extensions/pi-config-sync/index.ts. When adding a new skill authored by the user, update this allowlist and manifest managedRoots/managedFiles accordingly.

For hs-web-app Wayfinder planning, default to local Markdown under .wayfinder/ as used previously. Before writing even local map/ticket files, present the proposed map and ask for explicit approval and location confirmation. Never infer GitHub publication approval from discussion approval, `proceed`, existing labels, or gh availability.
